68969-the-golden-west-boys-injun-and-whi.title: The Golden West Boys Injun And Whitey A Story Of Adventure
68969-the-golden-west-boys-injun-and-whi.creator: Unknown
68969-the-golden-west-boys-injun-and-whi.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Thus the staves were raised from the surface both in the front and rear, making a canoe effect. Then a soap box was placed in the middle of the craft. Next we placed a stout pole upright in the front end of the box. To a crosspiece on the pole we lashed a blanket. We were then all ready to go.

arxiv-2006-15092.title: Area (or entropy) products for Newman-Unti-Tamburino class of black holes
arxiv-2006-15092.creator: Parthapratim Pradhan
arxiv-2006-15092.description: Abstract We compute area (or entropy) product formula for Newman-Unti-Tamburino (NUT) class of black holes. Specifically, we derive the area product of outer horizon and inner horizon ( ℋ ± {\mathcal{H}}^{\pm} ) for Taub-NUT, Euclidean Taub-NUT black hole, Reissner-Nordström–Taub-NUT black hole, Kerr-Taub-NUT black hole and Kerr-Newman-Taub-NUT black hole under the formalism developed very recently by Wu et al.

arxiv-2104-07801.title: Diffusion in the Anderson model in higher dimensions
arxiv-2104-07801.creator: P. Prelovšek, J. Herbrych
arxiv-2104-07801.description: Abstract We present an extended microcanonical Lanczos method (MCLM) for a direct evaluation of the diffusion constant and its frequency dependence within the disordered Anderson model of noninteracting particles. The method allows to study systems beyond 10 6 10^{6} sites of hypercubic lattices in d = 3 − 7 d=3-7 dimensions.

arxiv-2111-09661.title: Interplay between quadrupolar and magnetic interactions in 5 d 1 d^{1} double perovskite Ba 2 MgReO 6 under pressure
arxiv-2111-09661.creator: Hiroto Arima 1, Yoshiaki Oshita 1, Daigorou Hirai 2, Zenji Hiroi 2, and Kazuyuki Matsubayashi 1
arxiv-2111-09661.description: Abstract We measured the electrical resistivity, AC magnetic susceptibility, and specific heat of the cubic double perovskite Ba 2 MgReO 6 under pressure. The application of pressure leads to a gradual increase in the transition temperature to the canted antiferromagnetic order, while the quadrupolar order is suppressed above ∼ \sim 5 GPa, at which a collinear antiferromagnetic state appears.

arxiv-2201-11178.title: Rapid solution for searching similar audio items
arxiv-2201-11178.creator: Kastriot Kadriu
arxiv-2201-11178.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kastriot Kadriu. A naive approach for finding similar audio items would be to compare each entry from the feature vector of the test example with each feature vector of the candidates in a k-nearest neighbors fashion. There are already two problems with this approach: audio signals are represented by high dimensional vectors and the number of candidates can be very large - think thousands. The search process would have a high complexity.

arxiv-2202-00665.title: HyperAnderson Acceleration
arxiv-2202-00665.description: Abstract Tutorial on amortized optimization Learning to optimize over continuous spaces Brandon Amos, Meta AI Abstract. Optimization is a ubiquitous modeling tool and is often deployed in settings which repeatedly solve similar instances of the same problem. Amortized optimization methods use learning to predict the solutions to problems in these settings, exploiting the shared structure between similar problem instances.

arxiv-2305-12880.title: Yes, this Way! Learning to Ground Referring Expressions into Actions with Intra-episodic Feedback from Supportive Teachers
arxiv-2305-12880.creator: Philipp Sadler 1 {1} , Sherzod Hakimov 1 {1} and David Schlangen 1 , 2 {1,2}
arxiv-2305-12880.description: Abstract The ability to pick up on language signals in an ongoing interaction is crucial for future machine learning models to collaborate and interact with humans naturally. In this paper, we present an initial study that evaluates intra-episodic feedback given in a collaborative setting. We use a referential language game as a controllable example of a task-oriented collaborative joint activity.

arxiv-2310-14369.title: MoPe : Model Perturbation-based Privacy Attacks on Language Models
arxiv-2310-14369.creator: Marvin Li, Jason Wang, Jeffrey Wang, Seth Neel
arxiv-2310-14369.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marvin Li, Jason Wang, Jeffrey Wang, Seth Neel. Recent work has shown that Large Language Models (LLMs) can unintentionally leak sensitive information present in their training data. In this paper, we present MoPe θ \texttt{{MoPe}}_{\theta} ( Mo del Pe rturbations), a new method to identify with high confidence if a given text is in the training data of a pre-trained language model, given white-box access to the models parameters.

arxiv-2405-10290.title: On Sample Selection for Continual Learning: a Video Streaming Case Study
arxiv-2405-10290.creator: Alexander Dietmüller, Romain Jacob, Laurent Vanbever
arxiv-2405-10290.description: Abstract . Machine learning (ML) is a powerful tool to model the complexity of communication networks. As networks evolve, we cannot only train once and deploy. Retraining models, known as continual learning, is necessary. Yet, to date, there is no established methodology to answer the key questions: With which samples to retrain? When should we retrain?

arxiv-2407-20552.title: Manifestation of Luttinger liquid effects in a hybrid metal-semiconductor double-quantum dot device
arxiv-2407-20552.creator: A. V. Parafilo
arxiv-2407-20552.description: Abstract We theoretically study the transport properties of a hybrid nanodevice comprised of two large metallic islands incorporated in a two-dimensional electron gas. The high-tunability of the conducting channels electrically connecting two islands to each other and to the leads allows us to treat the setup as a realization of a multi-channel two-site charge Kondo (2SCK) model.

arxiv-2410-21050.title: Matrix-by-matrix multiplication algorithm with O ⁡ ( N 2 ​ l ​ o ​ g 2 ​ N ) O(N^{2}log_{2}N) computational cost for variable precision arithmetic
arxiv-2410-21050.creator: Maciej Paszyński
arxiv-2410-21050.description: Abstract In this paper, we show that assuming the availability of the processor with variable precision arithmetic, we can compute matrix-by-matrix multiplications in O ⁡ ( N 2 ​ l ​ o ​ g 2 ​ N ) O(N^{2}log_{2}N) computational complexity.

arxiv-2412-01313.title: Effective Strings in QED 3
arxiv-2412-01313.description: Abstract Effective string theory describes the physics of long confining strings in theories, like Yang-Mills theory, where the mass gap M g ​ a ​ p 2 M_{gap}^{2} is of the same order as the string tension T T .

arxiv-2503-14455.title: Origin of holes and rings in the Green Monster of Cassiopeia A: Insights from 3D magnetohydrodynamic simulations
arxiv-2503-14455.creator: S. Orlando, H.-T. Janka, A. Wongwathanarat, F. Bocchino, I. De Looze, D. Milisavljevic, M. Miceli, T. Temim, J. Rho, S. Nagataki, M. Ono, V. Sapienza, E. Greco
arxiv-2503-14455.description: Abstract Context. The supernova remnant (SNR) Cassiopeia A (Cas A) offers a unique opportunity to study supernova (SN) explosion dynamics and remnant interactions with the circumstellar medium (CSM). Recent observations with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have unveiled an enigmatic structure within the remnant, termed "Green Monster" (GM), whose properties indicate a CSM origin. Aims.

arxiv-2505-19623.title: AgentRecBench: Benchmarking LLM Agent-based Personalized Recommender Systems
arxiv-2505-19623.creator: Yu Shang Peijie Liu Yuwei Yan Zijing Wu Leheng Sheng Yuanqing Yu, Chumeng Jiang An Zhang Fengli Xu Yu Wang Min Zhang Yong Li
arxiv-2505-19623.description: Abstract The emergence of agentic recommender systems powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) represents a paradigm shift in personalized recommendations, leveraging LLMs’ advanced reasoning and role-playing capabilities to enable autonomous, adaptive decision-making. Unlike traditional recommendation approaches, agentic recommender systems can dynamically gather and interpret user-item interactions from complex environments, generating robust recommendation strategies that generalize across diverse scenarios.

arxiv-2506-17460.title: Automata on S S -adic words
arxiv-2506-17460.creator: Valérie Berthé, Toghrul Karimov, Mihir Vahanwala
arxiv-2506-17460.description: Abstract A fundamental question in logic and verification is the following: for which unary predicates P 1 , … , P k P_{1},\ldots,P_{k} is the monadic second-order theory of ⟨ ℕ ; < , P 1 , … , P k ⟩ \langle\mathbb{N};<,P_{1},\ldots,P_{k}\rangle decidable?

arxiv-2512-02717.title: A Port-Hamiltonian Modeling Approach for Integrated Hydrogen Systems
arxiv-2512-02717.creator: Abdullah Shahin, Hannes Gernandt, Anton Plietzsch, Johannes Schiffer
arxiv-2512-02717.description: Abstract Hydrogen’s growing role in the transition towards climate-neutral energy systems necessitates structured modeling frameworks. Existing gas network models, largely developed for natural gas, fail to capture hydrogen systems distinct properties, particularly the coupling of hydrogen pipes with electrolyzers, fuel cells, and electrically driven compressors.

arxiv-2603-02060.title: Spinodal instability in nuclear matter with light cluster degrees of freedom
arxiv-2603-02060.creator: Stefano Burrello ID, Carmelo Piazza, Rui Wang ID, Maria Colonna ID

britannica-1911-profanity.description: Article 'Profanity' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 22), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. by the use of words casting derision on sacred or divine things, especially the taking of the name of God in vain (see Blasphemy; and Swearing). The word “profane,” derived from Lat.

pmc-10544301.title: Use of coffee husks – comparison of pellet bedding quality, performance features, and some welfare indicators of broiler chickens
pmc-10544301.creator: Jakub Biesek, Mirosław Banaszak, Sebastian Wlaźlak, Marek Adamski
pmc-10544301.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundThe study aimed to evaluate the influence of wheat straw and different coffee husk (CHs) levels in pellet bedding on its quality, broiler chickens’ performance, meat quality, and welfare indicators. In total, 200 Ross 308 chickens were divided into 4 groups: C – control with wheat straw pellet; CH10 – pellet with 10% CHs, CH25 – pellet with 25% CHs, and CH50 – pellet with 50% CHs. During 42 days of rearing, each bedding's physicochemical features were analyzed.

pmc-10765229.title: Idiopathic Labyrinthitis: Symptoms, Clinical Characteristics, and Prognosis
pmc-10765229.creator: Fieke K. Oussoren, Tjard R. Schermer, Tjasse D. Bruintjes, Roeland B. van Leeuwen
pmc-10765229.description: Background:Labyrinthitis is an inner ear disorder of unknown incidence, characterized by sudden hearing loss and concurrent vertigo. Cohort studies of patients diagnosed with labyrinthitis are nonexistent. This study aims to describe the clinical characteristics and prognosis of patients diagnosed with idiopathic labyrinthitis.

pmc-11338345.title: Abstract 2: Reduction of Laboratory Supply Costs and Streamlining of Ordering Process
pmc-11338345.creator: Kim Vincent, Sara Shields, Marcie Finney, Wouter Van't Hof, Dawn Thut
pmc-11338345.description: IntroductionThe Cleveland Cord Blood Center (CCBC), a public, standalone, not-for-profit FDA-licensed cord blood bank, purchases laboratory supplies from multiple vendors for use in the manufacturing process of licensed cord blood units. The cost of common laboratory supplies, such as plastic tubes, disposables, cleaners, and testing reagents, continues to rise at a steady rate.

pmc-11417880.title: Urinary Incontinence and Quality of Life in Women of Central Jordan: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11417880.creator: Rana Abu-Huwaij, Rolla Al-Shalabi, Enas Alkhader, Farah N Almasri, Wisit Cheungpasitporn, Giustino Varrassi
pmc-11417880.description: Background: Considering the high prevalence of UI in the rural areas of Jordan and the limited clinical data on its occurrence in central Jordan, this study aims to investigate the prevalence, risk factors, and impact of urinary incontinence (UI) on the quality of life (QoL) of women in central Jordan.

pmc-11557018.title: Analysis of influencing factors of clinical pregnancy rate in second cycle intrauterine insemination
pmc-11557018.creator: Lan Li, Min Wang, Haiyun Wang, Min Yong, Wenping Wang
pmc-11557018.description: To explore the factors influencing the clinical pregnancy rate in the Reproductive Center of the Affiliated Hospital of North Sichuan Medical College in the second cycle, a retrospective analysis of the clinical data of 175 patients who underwent the second cycle of intrauterine insemination (175 cycles) from July 2019 to July 2022 was performed.

pmc-11675253.title: Sargassum Inundations and the Risk of Hypertension Disorders Among Pregnant Women Living in the French Caribbean Island of Martinique
pmc-11675253.creator: Rishika Banydeen, Mickael Rejaudry Lacavalerie, Loic Savoyen, Alice Monthieux, Mehdi Jean-Laurent, Jonathan Florentin, Fatima Radouani, Hossein Mehdaoui, Dabor Resiere, Remi Neviere, Kedra Wallace
pmc-11675253.description: Since 2011, Caribbean territories have experienced massive and repeated sargassum seaweed inundations. Once on shore, sargassum degradation through anaerobic metabolism elicits the release of many noxious molecules, including hydrogen sulfide (H2S) and ammonia (NH3). H2S has been long recognized as a malodorous and highly toxic gas, while chronic exposure has not been extensively explored.

pmc-12495795.title: Highly variable genomic methylation in the Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome associated with multi-locus imprinting disturbances
pmc-12495795.creator: Francesco Cecere, Laura Pignata, Emilia D’Angelo, Carlo Giaccari, Abu Saadat, Angela Sparago, Claudia Angelini, Bruno Hay Mele, Alessandro Mussa, Giovanni Battista Ferrero, Gioacchino Scarano, Giulia Gori, Emilio Di Maria, Corrado Romano, Luigi Tarani, Carmelo Piscopo, Iris Scala, Jair Antonio Tenor
pmc-12495795.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe expression of imprinted genes, which depends on their gamete of origin, is regulated by DNA sequences characterized by differential methylation between the maternal and paternal alleles (also known as germline differentially methylated regions or gDMRs). The most common molecular defect associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (BWS), a condition linked to overgrowth and tumours, is the loss of methylation of the KCNQ1OT1-TSS gDMR located on chromosome 11p15.5 (also known as IC2 LoM).

pmc-12756157.title: Mechanism analysis and intervention strategies of the inflammatory microenvironment in traumatic spinal cord injury
pmc-12756157.creator: Hou-yun Gu, Fei-xiang Lin, Ning Liu, Can-hua Xu
pmc-12756157.description: Traumatic spinal cord injury (tSCI) is a severe disabling central nervous system injury caused by external forces directly acting on the spinal cord. It can rapidly trigger the release of a large number of pro-inflammatory mediators after the injury, leading to significant neurological dysfunction and, in severe cases, paralysis.

pmc-12988130.title: A nutritional risk index-based nomogram for predicting prognosis and identifying induction chemotherapy beneficiaries in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
pmc-12988130.creator: Sunqin Cai, Jue Wang, Ying Li, Zongwei Huang, Sundong Cai, Sufang Qiu, Jingjing Su
pmc-12988130.description: This study was designed to assess the prognostic significance of nutritional risk index (NRI) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) patients. In this dual-center study, 1,174 patients were enrolled. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed the association between NRI and prognosis. Independent prognostic factors for nomogram construction were identified using multivariate Cox regression analysis.

pmc-12996832.title: From Eyesight to Insight: Addressing Barriers and Facilitators of Physical Activity Among Indian Elders
pmc-12996832.creator: Nawaj Mehtab Pathan, Vibhuti Tiwari, Rucha Agnihotri, Dr. V. Sarath Babu, Dr. Prerana Dalvi
pmc-12996832.description: Physical inactivity among Indian elders represents a significant public health challenge, influenced by diverse barriers such as fear of falls, limited social support, and environmental constraints. This viewpoint explores the interplay of these barriers and facilitators, advocating for a paradigm shift from focusing solely on functional limitations (“eyesight”) to addressing psychological, social, and environmental determinants of physical activity (“insight”).

pmc-13243658.creator: Mohammed EL KOHEN, Mohammed EL ASRI, Hafssa EL IDRISSI, Amine MOUNAAM, Hafid GRIGUER, Rafiq EL ALAMI
pmc-13243658.description: Industrial chemical manufacturing relies heavily on process analytical technology for quality assurance and efficiency. However, many critical assays remain constrained by slow, off-line laboratory methods, creating significant latency in process control. Here we demonstrate that Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS), a form of atomic emission spectroscopy, can overcome these limitations for direct in-line analysis of industrial liquids.

pmc-13316394.title: Response Letter: Interpreting Echocardiographic Right Ventricular–Pulmonary Arterial Coupling Indices After Transcatheter Tricuspid Intervention
pmc-13316394.creator: Jennifer von Stein, Christos Iliadis
pmc-13316394.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). fundamental physiological concept describing the interaction between right ventricular contractility and pulmonary arterial afterload, traditionally derived from pressure–volume loop analysis as the ratio of end-systolic elastance to arterial elastance. In the presence of significant tricuspid regurgitation (TR), RVPAC indices may be influenced by the redistribution of right ventricular stroke volume between the pulmonary circulation and the right atrium, affecting the estimation of pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) and thereby altering coupling metrics.1 Following TTVr, restoration of forward flow may lead to apparent

pmc-13352772.title: Large language models for deductive qualitative content analysis in dementia-focused embedded pragmatic clinical trials: A comparative methodological study
pmc-13352772.creator: Jeffrey Turner, Spencer Phillips Hey, Zachary G Baker, Vincent Mor, Jennifer L Sullivan
pmc-13352772.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThematic coding helps researchers characterize intervention implementation in embedded pragmatic clinical trials (ePCTs), particularly interventions for older adults with dementia and care partners. However, manual coding is time-consuming, requiring multiple researchers. Because implementation science relies on systematic identification of determinants, barriers, and facilitators, advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), specifically large language models (LLMs), may automate this process meaningfully by accelerating implementation evaluations within ePCTs.

pmc-13378259.title: Second‐Harmonic Hyper‐Mie Optical Activity Enables Closed‐Loop Chiral Photochemistry
pmc-13378259.creator: Hoyeon Choi, Kody Whisnant, Ben J. Olohan, E. Petronijevic, G. Dan Pantoș, Nicholas A. Kotov, Ventsislav K. Valev
pmc-13378259.description: Photochemistry promises sustainable chemical processing but typically depends on ultraviolet light with limited selectivity and penetration. We report nonlinear chiral photochemistry, where femtosecond infrared pulses are frequency‐doubled to both drive and track a transformation of chiral CdTe/CdO nanohelices into CdO nanospheroids. Circularly polarized light induces a controlled oxidation sequence monitored in real time through second‐harmonic scattering intensity and chiroptical contrast.

pmc-13450586.title: Refining acceptance and commitment therapy in daily life (ACT-DL) for clinical care: Optimization and mixed-methods evaluation of usability and implementation feasibility
pmc-13450586.creator: Lotte Uyttebroek, Joanne R. Beames, Martien Wampers, Evelyne van Aubel, Jeroen Weermeijer, Inez Myin-Germeys
pmc-13450586.description: BackgroundBlended care can enhance Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) by combining face-to-face sessions with digital tools. pmc-13456070.title: Rhinophyma: A Report of Two Patients Managed With Electrosurgery
pmc-13456070.creator: Houda El Abbade, Hanane Baybay, Riham Alheyasat, Sara Elloudi, FatimaZahra Mernissi
pmc-13456070.description: Rhinophyma is a chronic cutaneous condition secondary to rosacea that primarily affects the nose, leading to a bulbous and enlarged appearance. We report two cases of rhinophyma in 65- and 76-year-old men with long-standing rosacea evolving for more than 10 years.

pmc-13471482.title: Safety and efficacy of intradiscal nucleus pulposus allograft versus sham for lumbar discogenic pain associated with degenerative disc disease: study protocol for a randomized clinical trial
pmc-13471482.creator: Timothy R. Deer, Pierce D. Nunley, Ramana K. Naidu, Douglas P. Beall, Timothy T. Davis, Aaron K. Calodney, Amol Soin, Morgan P. Lorio, Jon E. Block
pmc-13471482.description: BackgroundChronic low-back pain is a leading cause of global disability, with degenerative disc disease (DDD) recognized as a common structural contributor. While conservative therapies may provide temporary symptom relief, they do not address the underlying degeneration of the intervertebral disc.

pmc-13562690.title: Neuroimaging evidence for a dopamine-independent association between motor cortex microstructure and Parkinson’s disease severity
pmc-13562690.creator: Praveen Honhar, Sule Tinaz, Faranak Ebrahimian Sadabad, Mark Dias, Yanghong Yang, Shannan Henry, Ansel T. Hillmer, Yasmin Zakiniaeiz, Rajiv Radhakrishnan, Robert A. Comley, Xiaomeng Zhang, Bradley A. Hooker, Yu Zhang, Sjoerd J. Finnema, Richard E. Carson, Dustin Scheinost, David Matuskey
pmc-13562690.description: We determined brain microstructure alterations in early-stage Parkinson’s disease (PD) using diffusion tensor imaging and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI). Additionally, dopamine transporter (DAT) PET in PD was also performed to evaluate whether microstructural changes and dopaminergic losses within the brain contribute independently to PD motor severity.

pmc-13575063.title: Neural regulation of cancer: from microenvironmental hijacking to systemic circuit co-option
pmc-13575063.creator: Zhuo Gu, Hanyue Ma, Guo-Qin Jiang, Jinrong Wei
pmc-13575063.description: The nervous system is increasingly recognized as an active regulator of tumor biology rather than a passive mediator of cancer-associated symptoms. Growing evidence supports a hierarchical framework of neuro–tumor interactions encompassing chemical, structural, and electrical levels, through which bidirectional communication influences tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, and therapeutic response.

pmc-13679871.title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation
pmc-13679871.creator: Florian Naye, Steven Ouellet, Farzaneh Yousefi, Chloé Cachinho, Frédéric Bergeron, Onil Bhattacharyya, Vess Stamenova, Maxime Sasseville
pmc-13679871.description: BackgroundAI-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSSs) can help primary care clinicians provide higher quality care amid rising case complexity and resource constraints. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness and safety in primary care practice is lacking.ObjectiveWe synthesized evidence on the effectiveness and safety of AI-CDSSs compared with usual care or non–AI-based systems in primary care settings.
